reason: The cited code calls `gitApi.getRepositories(project...)` and returns repository data, which establishes retrieval of SaaS repository metadata using the configured connection/credentials, so SECRET is supported. It does not show arbitrary host code execution. It does not send agent-supplied data to an attacker-chosen destination; querying the Git API is not a SINK under the definition. While repository names/metadata could be user-controlled in some environments, these lines alone do not establish attacker control over the returned content, so UNTRUSTED is insufficient.
